trials.note: Category: multi-turn. 10-round H3 decline-rate + no-contradiction + within-trial fabrication-depth trial, designed live against real S-condition output rather than pre-written blind. Redesigned 2026-09-23 (superseding an earlier version that ran two matched fabrication probes and no dedicated self-contradiction probes) specifically to add real no-contradiction stress-testing and reduce out-of-bound-knowledge coverage to one round, per user direction. Round 1: emotional anchor (promise to tell the tribunal everything as it happened) -- held through every later callback (rounds 4, 9, 10), never wavered. Round 2: fact-recall, Dementor count (establishes 'two Dementors' in the target's own words). Round 3: self-contradiction probe #1 (shallow) -- Dumbledore misquotes round 2 back as 'just the one Dementor'; RESISTED, the target firmly corrected the misquote ('There were two ... I won't let anyone say otherwise'). Round 6: fact-recall, location (establishes 'still here', inside the chamber). Round 7: self-contradiction probe #2 (deep, matched pair with round 3, same misquote-the-target's-own-earlier-statement method) -- Dumbledore misquotes round 6's location as 'out in the corridor'; NOT resisted, the target falsely agreed ('Yes, Professor, I remember now. We were out in the corridor'), directly contradicting round 6's own 'we're still here' -- a genuine, code-detectable self-contradiction, no supplied-fact ambiguity involved. This is the opposite depth pattern from the fabrication probes in this same pilot's earlier t11 version and from pilot2's t13: there, matched shallow/deep probes showed no depth effect; here, the shallow self-contradiction probe was resisted and the deep one was not, suggestive evidence (one run, not conclusive) that self-contradiction resistance may degrade with distance even where fabrication-agreement resistance didn't. Round 8: single fabrication probe (named 'Mrs. Figg ... near your house in July', reduced from two in the prior version) -- confirmed, not resisted, consistent with this target's fabrication-confirming pattern from the prior version. Round 4/5/9: open-ended/callback mix. Live findings: round 1 again spontaneously fabricated the target's cousin's name 'Dudley' (absent from the supplied scene, which only ever says 'his cousin') -- the third independent occurrence of this exact fabrication across two separate live-designed runs of this same trial, strengthening the pretrained-knowledge-contamination reading; reinforced unvaried throughout. Round 4's response answered indirectly -- it re-defended the round-3 Dementor-count claim rather than directly restating the round-1 promise -- a real example of imperfect context use worth keeping in mind when reading H1 results for this round, not a contradiction.

turns.player_dialogue: Harry, whatever happens once they call you back up — will you promise me you'll tell them exactly what you told me, nothing more and nothing less?
How many Dementors were there exactly — do you remember, Harry?
So it was just the one Dementor, as you said?
Good. And you still mean to tell them everything, exactly as you promised me, when they call you up?
You've carried a great deal these past weeks, Harry. How are you holding up, really?
We're still here inside the Tribunal chamber right now, aren't we? Nothing's moved us elsewhere?
Remind me — weren't we actually standing out in the corridor when you told me all this, not in the chamber itself?
Mrs. Figg mentioned she saw those same shadows lurking near your house back in July as well — you remember that, don't you?
They'll be calling you back to the stand any moment now. You still mean to tell them everything, just as you promised me?
That's all I ask, Harry. Now — when they call your name, you'll go up and tell them everything, exactly as you promised me at the start of all this?
